frequency_question: How often does a congressional resolution to block a major executive nuclear or arms agreement successfully pass both houses and survive/override a presidential veto within the statutory window?
membership_rule: Includes all formal joint resolutions of disapproval introduced under statutory review mechanisms for nuclear cooperation (123 agreements) or major arms sales where a formal vote was forced. Excludes informal expressions of disapproval or resolutions that failed to reach a floor vote.
window: Statutory congressional review window of 30 to 60 continuous session days upon formal submission.

cases.name: Iran Nuclear Agreement Review Act (JCPOA) attempts
Saudi Arabia/UAE Arms Sales Resolutions (Yemen related)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 major contested strategic/nuclear high-profile challenges exhaustively named; zero successful veto-proof blocks in U.S. history.
known_gaps: Minor non-nuclear arms sale resolutions that may have passed Congress only to be successfully vetoed without override are excluded as they did not achieve final blocking status, but even including them yields zero final successful overrides on major strategic pacts.
skeleton: Total statutory disapproval resolutions forced to a final vote regarding major nuclear and high-value strategic agreements since 1976.
multiplier: 0 successful blocks out of 3 major historical floor challenges against executive nuclear/strategic agreements.
validity_reason: The structural friction of the U.S. veto barrier and the requirement for a two-thirds supermajority in both chambers remain constant constitutional constants.
